run.question:
My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

Global Instructions
* Always check service dependencies first
* Verify environment variables are set correctly
* Check logs for error patterns before investigating further
* Contact the interlock team on all issues that could be related to STRIPE or the Stripe API
* On all other issues contact the capricorn team

report.summary: Checked the signup failure in namespace app-162 (this is a separate stack from the otel-demo services). Both signup-service pods (signup-service-7c89545dc9-57984, signup-service-7c89545dc9-5gs78) are Running with restartCount 0 and lastState empty, but Ready=False / ContainersNotReady; their logs repeat 'ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' and 'GET /ready 503'. Tracing that dependency: the payments-service pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-q7mkc logs 'ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail' and 'ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key', serves /ready and /health with 503, and its Endpoints object lists the pod only under notReadyAddresses (no ready address), which explains the connection refused seen by signup. The payments-service Deployment sets STRIPE_API_KEY from secretKeyRef payments-secrets/stripe-api-key, so the faulting configuration lives in that Secret; the Secret value itself cannot be read, so the key value is unverified and the conclusion is partial. Ruled out as causes: pod crashes/OOM/eviction (no restart, empty lastState, no Evicted/OOMKilled events), NetworkPolicy (none exist cluster-wide), ResourceQuota (none exist). Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable in this Run, so no metric or trace evidence was available. Runbook signup-service-debugging-runbook was fetched: step 1 (signup status/logs) done, step 2 (payments health/logs) done, step 3 (exec curl tests) could not be run because no exec/command tool is available - connectivity was instead inferred from the Endpoints object and the signup error log, step 4 (Stripe key and DB log greps) done for Stripe; no database/postgres errors appeared in the logs read, step 5 (env var inspection) partially done - Deployment env references were read, but Secret values are unreadable.

claims.text: Both signup-service pods in namespace app-162 (signup-service-7c89545dc9-57984 and signup-service-7c89545dc9-5gs78) are in phase Running with restartCount 0 and an empty container lastState, yet Ready=False and ContainersReady=False with reason ContainersNotReady.

signup-service-7c89545dc9-57984 logs repeat '2026-11-23 16:06:58 ... ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' followed by 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503', repeating at 16:07:03 and 16:07:08.

The second signup pod signup-service-7c89545dc9-5gs78 logs the same failure: 'ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' with 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503' at 16:06:58, 16:07:03 and 16:07:08.

payments-service pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-q7mkc logs '2026-11-23 16:06:54 ... ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail' and '2026-11-23 16:07:02 ... ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key', while serving 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503' and 'GET /health HTTP/1.1" 503'.

The payments-service Deployment in app-162 defines STRIPE_API_KEY via valueFrom.secretKeyRef {name: payments-secrets, key: stripe-api-key}, plus DATABASE_URL from secret payments-secrets/database-url and PORT=8080; the signup-service Deployment defines PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080.

The Endpoints object for Service payments-service contains only a notReadyAddresses entry for pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-q7mkc (10.244.0.34:8080) and no ready address, so the Service has no ready backend to accept connections.

Both Deployments in app-162 are new: payments-service created 2026-11-23T16:06:52Z and signup-service created 2026-11-23T16:06:51Z, each at generation 1, each with condition Available=False reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, and each last applied by manager kubectl-client-side-apply.

Payments-service pod readiness is determined by httpGet /ready on port 8080 every 5s (failureThreshold 3) and liveness by httpGet /health on 8080 every 10s; the pod itself answers those paths, returning 503, so the probe endpoint is reachable and the application is rejecting it.

Cluster events in the window group to only Normal reasons in namespace app-162: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet (2), Pod Created/Pulled/Scheduled/Started (3 each), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate (3); no Evicted, OOMKilled, Failed or Unhealthy events appear for these pods.

The most likely root cause is that the secret object payments-secrets in namespace app-162 holds an invalid Stripe API key under key stripe-api-key; payments-service loads it, its /ready and /health checks then fail (503 / 'Invalid Stripe API key'), the pod never becomes a ready endpoint, and signup-service's readiness check to http://payments-service:8080 is refused, making signup unready so users cannot register. The key value itself could not be read, so the invalid value is asserted only from the application's own log line.
NetworkPolicy blocking traffic to payments-service is rejected: a cluster-wide read of networkpolicies returned no objects, so no policy exists that could refuse the signup-to-payments connection.
Resource quota exhaustion as the cause is rejected: a cluster-wide read of resourcequotas returned no objects, and the payments pod schedule/started normally with exit-free containers.

Pod crash-looping, OOMKill or eviction as the cause is rejected for both workloads: all three app-162 containers report restartCount 0, an empty lastState, and PodScheduled/Initialized True, with only Normal Created/Pulled/Scheduled/Started events and no OOMKilled or Evicted reason.

Checked and not the failing dependency: the otel-demo deployments (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) each report 1/1 ready and available; signup-service's declared dependency is payments-service (PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL), not the otel-demo 'payment' service.

Follow the signup-service-debugging-runbook order: keep payments-service as the first dependency to check, and correct the Stripe key material used by payments-service - i.e. replace the value under key stripe-api-key in secret payments-secrets in namespace app-162 with a valid key (deployment spec expects that secret/key) and then let the payments-service pods re-read it via a rollout, since a config-only change keeps the same image python:3.11-slim.

Because the failure is Stripe-related, route it to the interlock team per the standing instruction (Stripe/Stripe API issues) rather than the capricorn team, and have them verify the key in payments-secrets against the Stripe account; also confirm signup-secrets/database-url and payments-secrets/database-url values, which are only references in the Deployment spec and could not be read.

gaps: Secret values cannot be read: the actual STRIPE_API_KEY in secret app-162/payments-secrets (key stripe-api-key) and DATABASE_URL in payments-secrets/signup-secrets were not verifiable, so the invalid-key finding rests only on the payments-service log lines.

Prometheus was unreachable in this Run (execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_label_values and list_prometheus_rules all returned source errors), so no error-rate, latency or transaction metric (for example app_payment_transactions_total, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count) was checked; ERROR/latency series for signup-service and payments-service are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable (traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span-level error or duration evidence exists for signup-service or payments-service, and the exact trace service names for them could not be compared with the Jaeger service list.

No exec/curl capability exists in this Run, so runbook step 3 (direct connectivity test from a signup pod to payments-service:8080) could not be executed; reachability was characterised only from the Endpoints object and the signup application error log.

No change-history integration is configured (not_integrated: change_history), so who or what changed the Stripe key material and when it changed cannot be determined; the Deployments themselves were applied by kubectl-client-side-apply at 16:06:51-16:06:52Z, only seconds before the observed failures, but the timing of the key change is unknown.

Only one payments-service replica exists, so there is no healthy sibling to compare against; log evidence for payments-service covers 16:06:54-16:07:08Z only (plus 4 lines outside the window that were dropped).
next_steps: Verify and correct the value of key stripe-api-key in secret app-162/payments-secrets (human check; secrets are not readable by this investigation), then roll the payments-service Deployment and confirm its /ready returns 200 and its pod appears under ready addresses in the payments-service Endpoints.

After payments-service becomes ready, confirm both signup-service pods return 200 on /ready and that their 'Payments service check failed' lines stop, then attempt a real signup/registration request to validate user impact is cleared.

Runbook signup-service-debugging-runbook steps 3 and 5 to completion in an environment with exec/kubectl access: curl -v http://payments-service:8080/health from a signup pod, and env inspection inside the payments pod for STRIPE_* and DATABASE_* variables.

Bring Prometheus and Jaeger endpoint availability back for this target and re-check error rate/latency for signup-service and payments-service, plus any alert rules referencing them, before certifying recovery.
Escalate the Stripe key handling to the interlock team per the global instruction, and ask for the change record for payments-secrets/Stripe key rotation to replace the missing change_history data.
